question: What physical exam finding tells you a miscarriage is threatened rather than inevitable?
explanation: A closed cervix means the pregnancy tissue is still inside the uterus. This is the main sign that separates a threatened miscarriage from one that cannot be stopped. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why does vaginal bleeding happen when a pregnancy is threatened?

options.A: Partial detachment of the membrane from the uterine wall
options.B: Severe bacterial infection destroying the cervical tissues
options.C: Complete rupture of the amniotic sac inside the cavity
options.D: Rapid hormonal withdrawal causing full shedding of the lining

explanation: When the membranes pull slightly away from the inside of the uterus, tiny blood vessels tear, causing the bleeding you see on the outside. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the most common reason for bleeding and loss in early pregnancy?

options.B: Heavy physical labor by the pregnant woman

explanation: Most first-trimester pregnancy losses happen because of natural genetic mistakes during cell division, not because of anything the mother did. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a risk factor for a threatened miscarriage?
explanation: Going to antenatal clinics helps protect the pregnancy and keeps both mother and baby healthy. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h2)

question: What kind of tummy discomfort does a woman with a threatened miscarriage usually feel?

options.A: Absolute absence of any sensation or discomfort
options.B: Mild, dull lower abdominal aches or back pain
options.C: Sharp, stabbing pains localized to the right iliac fossa

explanation: Unlike active labor, uterine activity is very low here, causing only mild aches or back pain instead of severe cramps. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h3)

question: A woman at 10 weeks has light spotting, a closed cervix, and normal vital signs. What is your best first nursing step?

options.A: Send the patient home immediately without any further evaluation
options.B: Immediately perform a surgical evacuation of the uterus in the ward
options.C: Administer high-dose oxytocin infusion to encourage quick delivery
options.D: Reassure the patient and assess vital signs while preparing for an ultrasound scan

explanation: When a patient is stable, stay calm, check her vitals, and arrange for an ultrasound to see if the baby's heart is beating. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which test tells you the most about whether the baby is okay during early bleeding?

options.A: A single routine urinalysis strip test
options.C: Abdominal girth measurement using a tape
options.D: Digital pelvic examination of the cervix

explanation: An ultrasound lets you look right at the embryo to check for a heartbeat, which is the surest sign the pregnancy is holding on. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do we check blood grouping and Rh factor for a woman with a threatened miscarriage?

options.A: To determine if an Rh-negative mother needs anti-D immunoglobulin
options.B: To measure the exact volume of blood lost during the bleeding episode
options.C: To check if the patient has a severe underlying blood infection
options.D: To calculate the exact gestational age of the developing fetus

explanation: If an Rh-negative mother bleeds, her blood might mix with the baby's. Giving anti-D prevents her immune system from reacting against future pregnancies. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main goal of care when a woman has a confirmed threatened miscarriage?

options.A: Immediately empty the uterine cavity using surgical instruments
options.B: Provide supportive care and monitor the progress of the pregnancy
options.C: Induce strong uterine contractions to speed up the miscarriage
options.D: Permanently suppress all natural maternal hormone production

explanation: Many of these pregnancies continue just fine. The focus is on keeping the mother comfortable and watching to see how things progress. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why don't we force strict bed rest anymore for every threatened miscarriage?

options.A: Modern evidence shows it does not prevent pregnancy loss and increases clot risks
options.B: It causes the cervix to dilate prematurely before 20 weeks
options.C: It completely stops the natural production of human chorionic gonadotropin
options.D: Patients refuse to stay in the hospital ward for long periods

explanation: Making a patient stay in bed doesn't stop a miscarriage, and it raises the danger of blood clots forming in her legs. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h5)

question: How does talking kindly and counseling a woman with a threatened miscarriage help her?

options.A: It guarantees that the pregnancy will go to full term safely
options.B: It reduces her anxiety and helps her understand what to expect
options.C: It physically stops the detachment of the placenta inside the womb
options.D: It replaces the need for any form of ultrasound examination

explanation: Clear and kind words take away a lot of fear, helping the mother feel supported and informed during a stressful time. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h6)

question: A patient feels guilty, thinking her farm work caused her bleeding. What should you tell her?

options.A: Tell her to stop thinking about the pregnancy and focus on other chores
options.B: Ignore the comment because psychological feelings do not affect healing
options.C: Agree with her and scold her for engaging in strenuous physical labor
options.D: Gently reassure her that everyday activities do not cause genetic or placental issues

explanation: Clearing up misunderstandings with kindness takes away unfair self-blame and builds trust between you and the patient. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h6)

question: What dangerous condition must you always rule out when a woman has early bleeding and severe pelvic pain?
explanation: An ectopic pregnancy can look like a normal early bleed but can cause life-threatening internal bleeding if missed. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h7)

question: At a primary health clinic, when should you immediately refer a bleeding patient to a bigger hospital?

options.A: Mild fatigue reported after a routine morning walk
options.B: Heavy bleeding soaking multiple pads with signs of shock
options.C: Normal blood pressure and regular fetal heart sounds
options.D: A single spot of brown discharge with a closed cervix

explanation: Heavy bleeding and signs of shock mean the patient needs urgent medical help and blood transfusions that only a larger hospital can provide. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h7)
